evidence.text: On the Q2 call management lowered its estimate of the full-year coding/WISeR revenue hit to $120-130M and said it would decline sequentially, yet kept the FY revenue range essentially unchanged ($835-875M, low end +$10M only), and an analyst on the call flagged that the lower impact estimate with an unchanged guide implies a cushioned second half; the Street sits at ~$844M, in the lower half, so a raise of the low end/narrowing upward is the plausible guide action and the one line this stock has repeatedly traded on.

The mirror risk (WISeR still in force for Q4, so management holds the range) is filed as its own small negative below.
evidence.independence: Shares the Q2 call with the reported-quarter finding (one document). Nyxoah's 2026-10-19 prelim, a direct competitor that reported after INSP last spoke, cut its own guide on a slow US ramp, which reduces the share-loss risk to INSP's Q4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001857190/000110465926117415/tm2627823d1_ex99-1.htm).

evidence.text: The Q3 call is where Inspire gave its first next-year outlook last year (Q3 2025: preliminary 2026 growth of 10-11%), and the 2027 backdrop it would guide against includes CMS's proposed CY2027 facility rates for HGNS of $35,414 HOPD (+12%) and $31,722 ASC (+15%) with physician 64582 at $699 (-4%), which management said on the Q2 call it was NOT yet assuming, plus ~$30M of Project Horizon savings to be reinvested in growth; there is no sourced 2027 Street number, so the bar is unknown.

evidence.why_not_priced: No 2027 revenue consensus is published (searched), so the market has no visible anchor for the first outlook; if the facility-rate increases were priced as upside, a Hold consensus and a ~$68 average target would not sit at spot. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Journavx came in just short of expectations ($19.6M) and Casgevy missed ($16.9M against a $35M model); the stock moved -1.0% close-to-close (https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/vertex-confident-journavxs-launch-despite-falling-short-sales, https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move).

evidence.independence: Same Q2 call; the Q2 release confirms the revenue and script figures (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). No Q3 IQVIA script data was found.

evidence.text: Casgevy has had three straight quarters of more than 100 patient initiations (through Q2 2026). H1 2026 infusions already exceeded all of 2025, Q2 revenue was $76.4M (+78% sequential), and the CFO said Casgevy is the larger contributor to the 'very confident' $500M+ non-CF target. That needs about $300M in H2 against about $200M in H1. The initiation backlog supports another sequential step in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Casgevy missed in Q3 2025 ($16.9M) and the stock moved -1.0%. Q2 2026's Casgevy acceleration came with a +1.7% move.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the $500M target is the headline every preview carries. What is not in the target is the initiation-to-infusion lag implying Q3 above Q2. Management says timing is variable, so the size is small. Net of the rest: Casgevy is about 2-3% of revenue.
evidence.independence: 247wallst repeats the initiation and pediatric-approval figures (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/the-500-million-non-cf-factor-vertex-investors-cant-ignore-on-nov-2/). It shares the call source with the Journavx finding, but they are different products.

evidence.text: The first FY26 guide to include Crinetics (closed 2026-09-01) will add Palsonify revenue (Crinetics Q2 2026 net product revenue $24.0M, Q1 $10.3M, so about $35-40M for Sep-Dec). What is not priced is the size: with FY consensus disputed ($13.06bn against $13.26bn), nobody has a clean rebased bar. Financing question answered: the loan buys a marketed product (Palsonify) and a Phase 3 asset; it is not distress.
